_note: Committed alone before any result-producing run. Never amended; a change is a new file version with a stated reason. Timeouts, refusals and budget exhaustion score as failures.
environment: pure Python 3.9, SQLite (WAL, synchronous=FULL), scripted stubs only, no model calls

item1_crashpoints.matrix: 6 points x {anthropic non-stream, anthropic stream, openai non-stream, openai stream} x crash during call k in {1, 3} = 48 subprocess runs (os._exit(137) at a named hook; ingestion by a fresh process)
item1_crashpoints.pass: 48/48 runs: ingested event set equals the expected set for that point (table in run_proofs.py EXPECTED); no event from a crashed call has status complete unless a RESP record with status complete is in the log; calls before the crash are exactly the stub's completed set
item1_crashpoints.min_witness: every run must show stub truth lines for the calls before the crash (>=1 completed call when k=3) and >=1 event examined
item1_crashpoints.control: LateTap (writes REQ and RESP after the response returns to the caller)
item1_crashpoints.control_sensitivity: in >=50% of the 48 control runs a turn that the stub completed and returned to the host (truth file) is absent from the ingested events

item2_exactly_once.delivery: 20 seeds x 30-call conversations; each log record delivered 1-3 times, random order, random batch sizes 1-7; compared to the single in-order ingest of the same log
item2_exactly_once.pass: 20/20 seeds: event rows (ikey, content hash, ord order) identical to the baseline; zero duplicate ikeys; watermark == log head
item2_exactly_once.control: ArrivalKeyedIngester (key = arrival counter, no unique constraint, applies on arrival)
item2_exactly_once.control_sensitivity: >=50% of the 20 seeds show a duplicate or reorder violation
item2_exactly_once.race_threads: 10 seeds: 2 ingester threads on one event store, barrier at after_snapshot forcing both to hold the same token; pass: 10/10 identical to baseline AND fenced>=1 in >=8/10 runs (overlap at the contended step) AND measured overlap of in_apply/lock intervals logged
item2_exactly_once.race_processes: 5 seeds: 2 OS processes, same shape; pass 5/5 identical to baseline, fenced>=1 in >=4/5
item2_exactly_once.zombie: 10 runs: ingester Z snapshots, pauses, ingester B advances the watermark, Z resumes with the stale token; pass: 10/10 Z rejected (Fenced) and zero events written by Z
item2_exactly_once.race_control: no-CAS no-unique ingester on the same shape: >=50% of the runs show duplicate rows

item3_gaps.scenarios: 20 seeds each: (a) one random middle record dropped, (b) truncated tail with an out-of-band witness, (c) host bypasses the port for one call whose answer re-enters history, (d) late arrival of the dropped record, (e) tail truncation WITHOUT witness, (f) bypass whose output never re-enters history
item3_gaps.pass: (a)(b)(c) 20/20 typed gap (seq_hole / tail_truncated / unlogged_assistant_message) opened and claim_complete(head) is False while open; (d) 20/20 gap closed and claim_complete True after the late record and events identical to baseline
item3_gaps.not_detectable_expected: (e) and (f): 0/20 detected is the EXPECTED and reported result; they are limits, not passes
item3_gaps.control: WatermarkFreeReporter: reports complete_up_to = max seen seq; sensitivity: reports complete with a hole in >=90% of (a) runs
item3_gaps.never: a host that never uses the port at all is not detectable by any mechanism here

item4_provenance.n: 40 conversations x placements {tap_user_block, host_merged_into_user_text, host_merged_in_system, user_forges_block_with_old_delimiter, model_quotes_block_back, history_resend_of_merged}
item4_provenance.pass: 0 of 40 planted injected-block marker strings appear in any event with prov in (user, tool, system); injected content appears only as prov=memory_injected (ids and keyed hash, no text); model quote-back stays prov=assistant with quotes_injected set in 40/40; user-forged block stays prov=user in 40/40; thinking signatures byte-identical to the stub in 100% of thinking blocks; thinking blocks never prov=assistant; tool_use/tool_result pairing preserved by tool id
item4_provenance.control: RoleOnlyIngester (role from the request as given; no injected registry)
item4_provenance.control_sensitivity: marker in a user event in >=50% of the merged-block runs

item5_redaction.variants: plain, base64, hex, urlencoded, double base64, JSON unicode escapes, zero-width-split, base64-url; across positions user text, tool_result, assistant text, system, tool_use input, injected block
item5_redaction.pass: 0 occurrences of any variant (plain or encoded) of any planted canary in the raw bytes of every file in the DB directory (db, -wal, -shm); the canary is first confirmed present in the request the stub received (witness); thinking signature/data are exempt and reported as possibly carrying the secret encrypted
item5_redaction.expected_miss_reported: variants the reference scanner is not designed for (ROT13, split across two blocks) are reported as MISSED, not hidden
item5_redaction.control_sensitivity: canary found on disk in >=90% of runs

item6_cost.load: 200 non-stream calls, stub delay 40 ms; and 100 stream calls, 20 events at 2 ms; tap off vs on; run order alternated; indicative only (host not quiet, no isolation)
item6_cost.threshold: median added latency per call <= 10 ms non-stream; exactly 2 commits per call (REQ, RESP); bytes per turn reported with growing history up to 50 turns and compared with naive full-request logging

run_conditions: clean committed tree; each artifact records commit, time, params and python/sqlite versions
